articleTitle: Bridging Language Barriers: An Open Source Typing Tool with a Vision for Indian Language Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: In an increasingly interconnected world, language diversity should be celebrated rather than hindered. This paper delves into the significance of open-source technology as a means of breaking down language barriers and promoting linguistic inclusivity. Focusing on the development of an open-source language typing tool, this research addresses a critical need in digital communication. While several commercial software solutions exist for language input, their proprietary nature limits accessibility and customization. In contrast, the proposed tool, crafted in Python, embraces the open-source ethos, fostering collaboration and allowing for tailored solutions to accommodate the unique linguistic nuances of Indian Languages. The core aim of this study is twofold. First, it seeks to establish a robust and user-friendly open-source input tool for Odia and Hindi with both Rule Based and free typing. Second, it lays the foundation for broader Indian language integration, recognizing the rich tapestry of languages spoken throughout the country.

articleTitle: Tea Leaf Disease Classification Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: A major contributor to India’s GDP and an integral part of the country’s agricultural sector is the tea production industry. It is now widely acknowledged that India is the leading consumer and number two producer of tea on an international scale. Lots of people rely on this industry as their main source of income, especially in rural areas, where it provides both direct and indirect work opportunities. There has been a dramatic increase in research into image recognition systems due to the meteoric climb of deep learning. This is especially true in fields like automated image classification and plant disease detection. The annual production of tea in India is substantial, which has been good for the economy. However, a major obstacle has emerged for the tea industry: the massive buildup of tea waste caused by tea leaf disease. If we want the sector to continue to thrive, we need to solve this problem. The total yield of the crop could be affected if illnesses slow down the growing rate of tea leaves. Making a CNN model that can detect diseases in tea plants is, hence, the main goal of this research. To do this, a dataset with numerous types of leaf photos will be used. CNN is a great fit for this application since it can rapidly assess many kinds of leaves, such as tea leaves and other plant leaves, which improves the accuracy of diagnostic results. Furthermore, the method under review has analyzed pictures of tea leaves and achieved an accuracy level of 92%. Furthermore, future updates will allow for even greater photo enhancement through the use of augmentation techniques, leading to even better results.

articleTitle: Customer Feedback Analysis using Customer Sentiment from Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is tapped as a crucial tool for driving insights into diverse domains. Through the rising volume of users’ content on online platforms, is now becoming a dominant tool. This paper precisely goes through the methods, applications, challenges, and latest improvements that SA is entailed with. It devotes itself to the multifarious aspects of SA, exploring different techniques of dealing with sentimental classification, opinion-spam detection, and assessing online reviews. It sheds light on the importance of the method of Aspect-Based Textual Analysis (ABSA) being used for the identification of sentiments directed to definite aspects or features of entities. This document demonstrates an extensive examination of some updated SA techniques such as lexical and then sophisticated machine learning approaches. It spells out the data collection tools, preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification models utilized in primary tasks (SA). Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes Classifiers, Random Forest Classifier and Feedforward Neural Networks are evaluated on both Bag of Words and TF-IDF vectorized data, the main mission being to show how they are applied in this intricate process. The research finds that the marketers of nearly all industries can benefit in every step of the decision process from product analysis to consumer insight by incorporating SA into their process.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Prediction using Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Heart disease continues to be the leading cause of death worldwide, necessitating the development of efficient and reliable predictive models to aid in early diagnosis and prevention. Traditional approaches to developing such models frequently encounter data privacy and scalability issues, especially when dealing with sensitive medical information spread across multiple institutions. Federated learning emerges as a promising approach for collaborative model training across decentralized data sources, eliminating the necessity for raw data sharing. In our research, we introduce a federated learning model to predict heart disease, drawing on insights from various hospitals or healthcare facilities while safeguarding data confidentiality. We employ a federated averaging algorithm to train a centralized model on locally stored patient data, ensuring that sensitive information remains secure within each participating entity. The proposed approach demonstrates competitive predictive performance compared to centralized models trained on pooled data, while addressing concerns related to data privacy and regulatory compliance. Through experimentation on real-world healthcare datasets, we validate the effectiveness and feasibility of our federated learning approach for heart disease prediction, paving the way for scalable and privacy-preserving predictive analytics in the medical domain.

articleTitle: Vehicle Security by Facial Recognition Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: In today's landscape, ensuring vehicle security is crucial, prompting the need for advanced solutions against theft and unauthorized access. This paper proposes integrating deep learning facial recognition with existing security systems to authenticate individuals for access. The approach leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and involves dataset collection, model training, real-time recognition, and system integration. The CNN model is trained extensively on diverse facial images to ensure reliability under various conditions. The paper addresses ethical and practical considerations, such as privacy protection and user acceptance. Ultimately, this fusion of facial recognition with CNNs offers a robust solution to enhance vehicle security and user experience, reducing the risks of unauthorized access and theft. Keywords: Vehicle security, facial recognition, real-time recognition, accuracy, privacy protection.

articleTitle: Real Time Bolt Segmentation on Diverse Backgrounds using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Bolts are vital components used in various structures to ensure stability and safety. Detecting bolts accurately is essential for structural health monitoring and maintenance across diverse backgrounds and environments. This paper aims to develop a real-time mobile application capable of robustly segmenting bolts in different settings using deep learning techniques. The proposed solution leverages the YOLO (You Only Look Once) framework, a powerful deep learning algorithm known for real-time object detection. This application holds potential for applications in industries such as construction, infrastructure inspection, and maintenance, ensuring the integrity and safety of structures in a wide range of scenarios. The proposed mobile based solution is able to detect the bolts with an mean average precision of 92.7%.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Computer Vision enabled GAN Model for Pest and Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Agriculture is among the most prominent occupation in India and among different parts of the globe, and plant diseases account for 35% of crop yield loss each year. Plants are affected by pests, environmental conditions, and nutritional deficits. Identifying and treating issues early is crucial for accomplishing desired yields. In this paper, an effective way for early detection of bugs in plants which combines Generative Adversarial Networks(GANs) with computer vision techniques is suggested. The proposed model utilizes advanced data augmentation, pre-processing, feature extraction, and classification to improve the precision of bug assessment in plants. Extensive set of simulations were performed to highlight the improved performance of the suggested approach. The experimental outcome has demonstrated promising results of the proposed model over the recent modern appraoches with maximum 95.2% accuracy, 92.6 % f-score, 93.8 % precision and 91.2% recall.

articleTitle: Maintaining Chain of Custody using Attribute Based Signcryption (ABSC)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: In the evolving digital world, the exchange of information or raw data has been so easy, but their security has been diminished due advancement in technology. Rate of cybercrime is increasing due to advanced technology which easily avails the required information to malpractitioners. This survey paper discusses the application and integration of attribute based signcryption by verifiable maintaining chain of custody and security of evidence. It helps to understand comprehensive overview of previous researchers and majorly highlight attribute based signcryption role in enhancing security and integrity of digital evidence. This elaborates challenges, pros, cons for using ABSC in chain of custody(CoC).

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Extractive Summarization Using NLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The step-by-step method of constructing a short, easy-to-read, understandable, and contextual summary of an extensive text document is called text summarization. The principal role is to acquire the correct amount of information within a period. Text reports are finished by humans, which requires experience in space and is also terribly tedious and time-consuming. Along with the advancement of technology, the amount of text data is difficult to understand and is not available in a structured manner due to the larger number of characters. Hence, this is a necessary tool for today. It has been divided into two subparts: text summarization with an abstractive approach, otherwise known as Abstractive Text Summarization (ATS), and the second, text summarization with an extractive approach, otherwise known as Extractive Text Summarization (ETS). In comparison to ATS, the second technique is significantly more manageable and efficient. ETS primarily operates by extracting essential tokens, and in some cases, entire sentences, from the input text document. Consequently, this approach autonomously generates a summary. This work has not only identified novel findings but also suggested cutting-edge techniques and approaches for future researchers in the field, offering valuable insights and practical support.

articleTitle: Predicting Election Outcome and Voting Trend with Generative Machine Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The present research gives extensive attitude towards using Gen AI for foretelling election results and also analyze the behavior of the voter while voting. By capitalizing various data sources from preceeding election outcomes, public polls, media reports and sometimes economic indicators Gen AI prepares as efficient and explained forecast. After crucial phases if data making, that includes normalization, cleaning and feature of engineering the method also involves the training and optimization also includes validation. The research also goes through ethical criteria such as fairness and privacy with efficient techniques for visualization, This method enhances the transparency and reliability of voter perception and also election forecasts.

articleTitle: Exploring Lightweight YOLOv8 Architectures for Circuit Board Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Modern electronics relies heavily on circuit boards, which must be designed and produced using a variety of procedures in order to be filled with electrical components. This procedure includes drilling and plating holes, applying masks, painting and etching fiberglass-reinforced epoxy resin boards, and adding components to the boards. Because of variations in the materials and processes, mistakes might occur at any stage. Traditionally, conductivity, impedance, and visual testing are used in a multi-stage approach to identify and resolve these problems. With modest hardware requirements, computer vision, especially using convolutional networks, provides considerable promise to improve defect detection. Once implemented, these models may significantly increase error detection and lower board failure rates, despite the significant hardware requirements for training. Using a publicly accessible dataset, this study investigates the use of the YOLO model for fault identification in circuit board fabrication. The YOLOv8 model’s lightweight design is examined; the medium-sized model achieves a mAP@50 score of 0.990, indicating that it considerably improves fault detection.

articleTitle: Crow Search Algorithm-Based Task Offloading Strategies for Fog Computing Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The rapid digitization of various aspects of life is leading to the creation of smart Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, where interconnected devices generate a significant amount of valuable data. These IoT devices face constraints such as limited computational resources and bandwidth. Cloud computing emerges as a solution by offering ample resources for offloading tasks efficiently despite introducing latency issues, especially for time-sensitive applications like Fog Computing (FC). Fog Computing addresses latency concerns by bringing computation and storage closer to the network edge, minimizing data travel distance, and enhancing efficiency. Offloading tasks to Fog Nodes (FNs) or the cloud can conserve energy and extend IoT device lifespan. The offloading process is intricate, with tasks categorized as full or partial, and its optimization presents an NP-hard problem. Traditional greedy search methods struggle to address the complexity of task offloading efficiently. A Modified Crow Search Algorithm (MCSA) has been proposed as a meta-heuristic optimization algorithm. MCSA aims to effectively optimize computation offloading, providing solutions to this challenging problem.

articleTitle: IoT based protective face cover with body and environment vital parameters monitoring system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: IoT-enabled healthcare systems can enhance the monitoring of patient well-being, particularly in remote distant regions with insufficient infrastructure, as IoT has extended its presence into the everyday lives of individuals, whether it's through remote communication, data transmission, or wearable devices tracking your location and health status, among other functions. The COVID-19 pandemic shook the otherwise stagnant healthcare system in such a way that there has been a resurgence in the demand for fast and reliable health monitoring systems. It reiterated that in today's unpredictable fast world, even otherwise nearly everyone, once they reach a certain age, should utilize health monitoring devices to gauge essential body parameters. Continuous real-time monitoring of a person's heart rate, body temperature and respiratory environment is imperative for ensuring their safety and well-being, particularly when working in underground mines, hospitals, refineries, and even while commuting in unfavorable polluted environment. In this research work, we introduce the design and development of a wearable monitoring head gear designed to consistently measure wearers heart rate, body temperature, and surroundings ambient gases, sending this data to a central monitoring station in real-time. It operates on a compact battery, capable of prolonged continuous operation thus making it robust and reliable apart from being more than 98% accurate.

articleTitle: Smart Farming Sloutions for Crop Disease Prediction and Control using IoT and ML
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The agricultural domain stands as a pivotal sector, underpinning not only economic stability but also fundamental human sustenance. Nowadays, it's challenging to get the right output from agriculture because crops are afflicted with multiple diseases during growth, which frequently require the farmer's notice, in the poor production of crops. Over a period of thousands of years, agriculture has changed by including new technologies and techniques that increase production, sustainability, and efficiency. This study focuses on new approaches to smart farming that combine machine learning (ML) and the Internet of Things (IoT) to predict and handle crop diseases and correction. The objective is to collect real-time data on crop conditions by utilizing IoT devices that relate to sensors for temperature, moisture, humidity, NPK, PIR and combine ML output with these readings. The input information is analyzed using machine learning (ML) methods to compare the effectiveness of ResNet50, VGG16, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in the management and prediction of disease. As per the analysis, ResNet50 performs more effectively compared to the other algorithms due to its lower loss, which indicates a more precise detection of diseases. shown in this work how IoT and ML can transform the farming process by giving farmers a more precise and efficient way of managing and monitoring crops.

articleTitle: Space-Time Attention Model-based Anomalous Event Classification for Smart City Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Anomalous event classification automatically identifies anomalous events using the videos in an intelligent video surveillance system. However, anomalous event classification is challenging due to inherent research challenges such as the requirement of high-end computational infrastructure, data imbalances, and data scarcity. Typically, a combination of Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long-Short-Term-Memory (LSTM) are used to model the spatiotemporal dynamics of the videos for video classification. However, these models have no attention mechanism to boost the relevant spatiotemporal features and discard the irrelevant features. Hence, a Space-Time Attention Model (STAM)-based anomalous event classifier is proposed. The model is trained and validated on the "Anomalous Event Classification 22," i.e., the "AEC22 dataset" comprising twenty-two anomalous event classes such as abuse, arrest, arson, assault, etc. The STAM is a combined spatial and temporal transformer that takes a series of frames extracted from the input video and predicts corresponding video-level classification as the output. Subsequently, the proposed model provides 92.84% classification accuracy, which is compared with the two state-of-the-art video classification methods to validate its superiority. The proposed model has huge potential for classifying anomalous events in smart city applications.

articleTitle: Content based texture image retrieval using Linear Discriminant Analysis and weighted distance metric
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: In the digital era, low-cost hardware like sensors and cameras has led to the creation of numerous image databases for various applications. This has led to the need for retrieval systems that rely on visual content, and these types of systems are called content-based image retrieval (CBIR) systems. It’s a method utilized to locate and extract digital images from extensive databases by considering their visual attributes, as opposed to relying exclusively on metadata or written descriptions. In order to obtain appropriate images from the database, features including colour histograms, texture patterns, and shape descriptors are being used to determine similarities between the images. Over the course of the last twenty years, efforts have been directed towards creating hand-crafted features tailored for CBIR systems. However, depending solely on distance-based retrieval methods is a formidable task. Hence, this study strives to leverage the capabilities of classifiers as well for the purpose of retrieval. So, the proposed CBIR paradigm uses not only the hand-crafted features but also the strength of the classifier with weighted distance metricTherefore, the proposed CBIR paradigm is designed in a way that it uses the strength of the NaiveBayes classifier to compute weighted distance using hand-crafted wavelet features to get similar images from the database. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on three most popular texture datasets and found to be better among all the methods reported in this work.

articleTitle: Soldier Monitoring and Tracking System using ESP-NOW and SMTP Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The paper introduces a Soldier Monitoring & Tracking System for real-time battlefield surveillance. Integrated with pulse sensors and GPS modules, soldiers' vital signs and locations are transmitted to a central base station via ESP32 microcontrollers. To address combat communication challenges, we utilize the ESP-NOW protocol for rapid message transmission within a 480-meter range. Additionally, soldiers can trigger distress signals, providing precise location and pulse rate information to nearby medical facilities. In emergency situations, SMTP protocol is used to send emails to hospitals. Through this integration of advanced technology, our system ensures efficient communication and enhances soldier safety in high-risk environments.

articleTitle: DL-Integrated Chatbot with GPS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: This paper presents the construction and integration of a deep learning-based chatbot with GPS functionality in order to deliver contextually appropriate and location-aware interactions. The chatbot can understand and generate content similar to that of a human by using advanced natural language processing (NLP) models, such as BERT and GPT. This improves user communication. With the use of GPS integration, the chatbot may obtain real- time location data, which allows it to tailor its responses to the user's geographical position. Our methodology included training the chatbot on many conversational datasets and fine-tuning its contextual understanding with location-specific data. In order to provide seamless communication between the chatbot and GPS, geolocation APIs were used to get accurate, efficeint and reliable location data. The system's performance was evaluated through extensive real-world testing, with a particular emphasis on the correctness and relevancy of the chatbot's responses. User input was obtained in order to assess satisfaction and pinpoint areas in need of development. Findings show that by providing precise, context-aware information, the integrated chatbot greatly enhances user experience. To further improve customer support, the chatbot also offers details about hotels, restaurants, and other well-known locations, along with precise addresses. All things considered, this work demonstrates the practical benefits of combining deep learning with geospatial technology, creating new opportunities for advanced applications in intelligent urban navigation, travel assistance, and customer support.

articleTitle: A Smart Security System Using IOT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The need for advanced security systems that combine maximum protection with user- friendliness has increased in the quickly changing world of today, especially for residential applications. Driven by the desire to safeguard their homes and loved ones from possible dangers, homeowners look for cutting-edge solutions that offer ease of use and safety. The project involves designing an intelligent security system. This system includes an automatic door lock mechanism. It also features an intruder alarm system. The system uses facial recognition technology for security is the main goal of this project. By using face recognition technology, the suggested system makes sure that only users who have registered are able to access it and keeps out illegal users. The intruder alarm system is set off in the event that security is attempted to be breached; it instantly notifies the relevant authorities, guaranteeing a timely reaction. The system incorporates Internet of Things (IoT) technology to improve user experience by allowing remote control and monitoring via Telegram and other platforms. The system's dependability and efficiency are guaranteed by the employment of a Wi-Fi module in conjunction with an Arduino-based microcontroller. This system greatly lowers the danger of theft and burglary in homes and buildings by integrating state-of-the-art face recognition technology with automatic alarms. It also offers consumers more convenience and peace of mind in addition to improving security.

articleTitle: Next-Gen Ophthalmic AI: Early Eye Disease Detection with ResNet-18
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Classifying eye diseases is an important issue for countries around the world. The goal is to use advanced computer methods, created from research, to improve old models. This will help us accurately identify different eye diseases by looking at photos. This paper used machine learning and computer vision techniques to sort images into four categories of eye problems: cataract, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and healthy eyes. In this study, we taught the ResNet-18 model again using a learning rate of 5x10^-5 for the ResNet-18 part and 8x10^-4 for the extra dense layers. Our model worked really well, with an overall accuracy of 86%. The model did a great job in identifying diabetic retinopathy cataract, showing strong accuracy and effectiveness in its results. However, other groups of people with glaucoma had much lower scores on these measures. These results strongly show that the model could help find, diagnose, monitor, and treat eye diseases early. This will be very helpful for people and their medical care. This will help society by improving the overall quality of medical care. Doctors and nurses everywhere are using these results as a guide to help provide good care at a fair price in the healthcare system.

articleTitle: Approximate squaring circuits for error-resilient applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Most approximation computing research focuses on arithmetic operations like binary multiplication, division, and addition. Squaring, another fundamental arithmetic operation, is commonly required. Allowing small errors can improve circuit performance, which is useful for error-tolerant applications. The recursive squaring approach, which employs approximate multipliers and squarers, reduces redundant computations, power consumption, delay, and area in computing circuits. This paper proposes a 4-bit approximate squarer P1, which is implemented in the recursive squaring methodology. In the comparison between the exact and approximate squares employed by the proposed squarer P1, it was observed that area decreased by 79.20%, power by 58.55%, and delay by 50.81%. Error metrics like error rate, MRED, and MNED are also analyzed and compared with exact squarer. The behaviour of the proposed configurations is tested using the amplitude modulation application. The designs are synthesized using Cadence Genus with a 90nm technology library.

articleTitle: Content Based Video Retrieval with Handcrafted Features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: With rapid growth of social media platforms and widespread use of handheld devices such as mobile phones and video cameras, the number of videos being captured and shared over the internet has increased significantly. However, due to the lack of organization, most of these videos lack semantic context. Traditional methods of video retrieval involve searching for relevant videos using attached semantics. which has led to the need for content-based video retrieval, where video contents are utilized for searching, whether by video or text queries.The primary goal of our system is to provide relevant videos from a database. Our proposed approach in this paper employs Pearson’s coefficient of correlation (PCC) for key frame extraction from videos, subsequently building a feature vector that represents the video’s content. We have also experimented with linear binary pattern (LBP) and Colour moments (CM). We have used precision metric for evaluating performance. For conducting experiments, we utilized the UCF101 dataset, comprising 13,320 videos across 101 categories.

articleTitle: Exploring Advanced Techniques for Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Detection in Social Media Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis and emotion identification in social media face big hurdles due to the informal and complicated language used there. Current approaches frequently suffer from problems including language, ambiguity, and sarcasm. In order to overcome these difficulties, this work presents the BERT + Fine-Tuned Classifier model, which makes use of BERT's sophisticated contextual knowledge. Preprocessing data, domain-specific tailoring, and real-time deployment are all part of the method, which aims to increase the precision and flexibility of social media text analysis. This solution gives a better framework for getting around the drawbacks of conventional techniques and gives a more efficient way to analyze sentiment and emotions in social media settings.

articleTitle: Smart House Management and optimized scheduling method for peak-hour demand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The IoT-based smart home management and control focuses on the effective utilization of electricity in the increased usage of devices in the modern era. The smart grid represents a transformative paradigm shift in modern power distribution systems, integrating advanced technologies to enhance efficiency, reliability, and sustainability. Central to this transformation are shiftable and non-shiftable electric devices, pivotal components in shaping the grid's operational dynamics. This abstract provides insight into the functioning and implications of shiftable and non-shiftable electric devices within the context of the smart grid. Shiftable devices allow for flexible energy consumption scheduling, optimizing resource utilization and load management, while non-shiftable devices maintain constant demand and require immediate power supply.

articleTitle: Exploring Strategies and Algorithms for Tackling Class Imbalance Across Varied Data Types
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: In the current internet era, data is widely dispersed across several domains. However, a large proportion of these datasets have unbalanced distributions, where some groups are obviously more common than others. This uneven distribution of data across multiple classes is one of the main problem for unbalanced learning, which makes it harder for classifiers to learn from classes present in smaller numbers. There are number of oversampling and undersampling techniques available to avoid this problem. Ensemble approaches like ADASYN, RUSBoost, and combining techniques like SMOTETomek are popular ways to deal with unbalanced data. We compared ADASYN, RUSBoost, and SMOTETomek on three real-world datasets. This paper explores the pros and cons of sampling techniques used to tackle imbalanced data in machine learning. We highlight key benefits such as improved model performance and reduced training time, while also addressing potential challenges like information loss and overfitting. We offer recommendations for choosing suitable sampling methods based on class distribution and model requirements. Through experiments with hybrid approaches at different levels of imbalance, we demonstrate that these strategies enhance the robustness of models, leading to better overall

articleTitle: An Intelligent Hybrid GenAI Model for Software Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Software Testing, a well-defined process and a major component of software development. It covers various methods such as execution of a software program, predicting errors, to meet user needs, and ensure that the system is working correctly. Due to the advanced development in technology around the world, new methods are introduced to test the software. This summary talk discusses the current state of the art of AI(Artificial Intelligence) for software testing. The purpose of software testing is validation, verifying and detection of errors. For the study, we explored around 30 articles from different research surveys. 12-15 articles were selected for the final review. Artificial intelligence(AI) which has emerged in a promising approach to software testing in recent years. The main aim of this paper was to review how Artificial Intelligence(AI) works in Software testing. This paper had also proposed many key offerings of AI in the upcoming future for the area of software testing.

articleTitle: Demystifying AI: A Robust and Comprehensive Approach to Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in various computing platforms and areas, necessitates the development of strong Explainable AI (XAI) techniques. Most current AI models are opaque about their decision-making process thereby impeding trust, debugging, and improvement. The goal of this research is to develop comprehensive robust XAI methods capable of explaining the reasoning and decision-making processes in Autonomic, Edge, Server-less, Quantum computing platforms and IoT, Business Automation, Service Innovation domains where these AI models are deployed.This study comprehensively addresses the opacity in AI models through solutions for balanced test-train splits, model evaluation, feature importance, metric imbalances, ROC curve and precision-recall curve analysis, accuracy and statistical metrics, benefits of manual review. This research aims at increasing transparency and trustworthiness within AI systems through developing as well as applying such XAI methods that can detect and mitigate biases while enhancing ethical debugging; responsible development for AI enabled computing purposes.

articleTitle: ECGText: Crafting Emotional Texts through GenAI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The generation of emotionally nuanced text is a growing area of interest in AI, particularly in enhancing human-machine interaction. This paper presents ECGText (Emotionally Cognizant Generation of Text), a novel model that integrates emotional intelligence into GPT-based text generation. The motivation behind this study stems from the limitations of current text generation models, which lack the ability to generate emotionally resonant content. By incorporating sentiment analysis and emotion recognition into the text generation process, ECGText produces emotionally appropriate outputs, enhancing engagement and relatability. Through comprehensive experiments and evaluations using diverse datasets, results demonstrate that ECGText outperforms baseline models in generating sentiment-rich text while maintaining coherence and fluency. This study advances the field of AI-driven communication, bridging the gap between machine-generated text and human emotional expression.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Deep Learning Framework for Accurate Leukemia Classification from Microscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Leukemia, a kind of blood cancer, is difficult to diagnose owing to its many varieties and sophisticated diagnostics. The traditional method of diagnosis is to examine blood and bone marrow samples under a microscope, which takes time. This work investigates the use of deep learning models—VGG16, EfficientNetV2, MobileNetV3, and Densenet121—to assist in recognizing leukemia cells in blood cell pictures. EfficientNetV2 proved to be the most successful model, with accuracy rates of roughly 99.41% in training, 96.19% in validation, and 96.07% in testing. Integrating these algorithms into diagnostic procedures has the potential to accelerate and increase leukemia detection accuracy. This innovation has the potential to revolutionize leukemia diagnosis, allowing for faster and more accurate detection of malignant cells. Ultimately, it may improve treatment results and patient care by allowing for speedier introduction of suitable medicines. This work represents a major advance in using technology to improve leukemia diagnosis and treatment options.

articleTitle: A Big Data Study: Efficient Facebook Data Analysis using Apache Hive and R for Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: This paper comprehensively analyzes Facebook data, a rich source of valuable information within big data. The study encompasses data collection, preprocessing, and exploratory analysis of a substantial dataset derived from Facebook interactions and activities. Through advanced data processing techniques and statistical methodologies, we unveil meaningful insights into user behavior, content engagement, and patterns on the platform. This analysis has significant implications for understanding user preferences, trends, and the dynamics of social networking in the digital age. The study revealed valuable trends, patterns, and metrics related to user interactions, posting habits, etc. Integrating Hive commands for data analysis and R programming for visualization offered a powerful synergy that made the findings accessible and visually compelling. The project underscores the importance of big data analytics in unraveling the hidden dimensions of social media and offers a practical demonstration of the power of data-driven decision-making. The findings and visualizations derived from this analysis shed light on the vast landscape of Facebook, enabling informed decisions and future research in social media analytics.

articleTitle: Smart System to Aid Dyslexia Reading through Audio Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Dyslexia affect approximately 10% of the population and has become the most common learning disability. There are significant disabilities in reading, writing and spelling. However, advances in technology have made it possible to support those struggling in new ways. One way to enhance these speech recognition skills is to develop a voice-activated Bluetooth module reading amplifier with built-in LED lights. articleTitle: Sleep Apnea Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: A promising strategy for improving sleep apnea detection and treatment is machine learning. articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Classify Skin Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: A effective treatment for skin cancer depends on early discovery, which may be a major around the world health issue. This study offers a interesting strategy for dependably classifying skin injuries as benign or malignant by utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are a promising strategy with incredible potential for skin cancer screening. CNNs are well-known for their capacity to observe complex designs from picture data and are able of accurately recognizing benign or malignant skin injuries. Analysts can make exceptionally valuable demonstrative devices by utilizing enormous datasets of skin injury photos to prepare CNN models. articleTitle: Fashion Recommendation System using ResNet50
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach towards fashion recommendation systems, exploiting deep learning techniques—especially the Residual Network (ResNet) architecture—to mine complex and essential information out of images. In this way, by employing Convolutional Neural Networks to analyze fashion images, the distance between user preferences and the available product catalog will narrow significantly, providing a much more personalized and relevant shopping experience. This line of work considers classical recommendation system shortcomings, which mostly end up not being able to reflect the deeply subjective and very complicated nature of fashion decision-making. The system advocates the application of ResNet50 for the extraction of features and uses the nearest neighbors algorithm in making recommendations with the aim of increasing relevance and accuracy of the suggestions while giving a completely good user shopping experience. Through these comparisons, the results of the experiment proved the effectiveness of the system in authentically giving the customer an individualized, enjoyable shopping experience and the effectiveness in applying deep learning to develop the fashion recommendation system.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network Analysis of Optometry Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: This survey explores the potential of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for analyse eye-trailling data, generally data obtained from Optometry systems. RNNs stand out at distinguishing patterns in consecutive data, making them appropriate for tasks like foretell future gaze, distinguishing areas of interest, and detecting anomalousness in gaze patterns. articleTitle: A Pragmatic Study on Various Approaches Used for Sarcasm Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Sarcasm is an intricate type of figurative language that presents a significant obstacle to sentiment analysis because it skillfully conveys negative feelings through words that appear positive or intensified, making classification more difficult. Sentiment analysis works well with plain language, but sarcasm is difficult to interpret precisely because of its complex structure. To tackle this problem, different approaches are used, such as integrating language cues into conventional techniques and utilizing deep learning's ability to extract complex patterns from large-scale datasets. New complexities are introduced by the rapidly changing digital language landscape, which calls for constant model adaptation to take into account dynamic expressions, slang that is still developing, and changing cultural contexts. This review paper offers an overview of previous works on automatic sarcasm detection, providing information on approaches, datasets, problems, and patterns in the field. It gives a thorough analysis of rule-based, deep learning, machine learning, and conventional methods, leveraging their distinct advantages to improve sarcasm detection. Additionally, the paper presents indicative performance metrics, discusses common tasks, and makes recommendations for future research.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fetal Care and Maternal Health with Machine Learning: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Fetal growth restriction and preterm delivery proceed to be major around the world wellbeing concerns, with serious consequences for the wellbeing of moms and babies. Provoke and exact estimating of these issues is basic for prompt action. In spite of the fact that progresses have been made in conventional clinical assessment approaches, the potential of computational apparatuses to back clinical decision-making is getting to be progressively clear. With its capacity to assess complex data patterns, machine learning (ML) has gotten to be a reasonable procedure for making strides pre-birth care. The review's conclusions highlight ML's potential to upgrade fetal care. Various examinations yielded empowering discoveries, as machine learning models outperformed routine risk evaluation instruments in terms of anticipated exactness. Numerous pregnancy issues, counting fetal growth limitation and untimely conveyance, have been viably anticipated by machine learning calculations. Healthcare experts can reduce unfavorable results by utilizing focused medicines to distinguish high-risk pregnancies early on. In any case, obstacles and confinements anticipate machine learning from being broadly utilized in restorative settings. Given that solid machine learning models require expansive and representative datasets, information accessibility and quality stay significant concerns. Future considers ought to concentrate on making and assessing machine learning models over a extend of demographics, improving the interpretability of models, and incorporating ML into clinical strategies. By handling these issues, machine learning (ML) has the potential to make strides the wellbeing of expectant women and their babies.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Resting-State EEG Patterns in Female Schizophrenia and Addiction Patients Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Machine learning aids in accurately diagnosing psychiatric disorders, impacting individuals' quality of life and society, by identifying and classifying them efficiently. Traditional diagnoses of psychiatric disorders relied on subjective assessments, which are time-consuming, costly, and human biased; machine learning offers faster, cheaper, and more accurate solutions. The aim of this study was to evaluate patterns of relationship in female schizophrenic and addictive disorder patients by the application of computational techniques to analyze resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data signals obtained via machine learning with a view to identify distinctive patterns or features that can help medical practitioners to differentiate between the two patient groups. The study utilized data on beta waves collected from the forehead of the human subjects with the electrodes in positions fp1 and fp2. A review of published literature in the field of diagnosis of mental health disorders using machine learning was also conducted in order to identify current trends on the subject and identify possible research gaps for further research. The results show the relationships between age, education, IQ, and AB.D.beta a.FP1/FP2 assessed using correlation coefficients and p-values show a weak negative relationship between age and AB.D.beta a.FP1/FPI/FP2. The correlation coefficients are -0.1054, -0.1722, and -0.0975, respectively. The p-values for these relationships are 0.6407, 0.4435, and 0.4962, indicating that the correlations are not significant. Age, education and IQ did not appear to have a significant impact on the AB.D.beta a.FP1/FPI/FP2 patterns in the studied female patients. Our study investigates the efficacy of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in diagnosing psychiatric disorders in females. We achieved an accuracy of 84.3% using CNNs for evaluating EEG patterns.

articleTitle: CliniLiver: Leveraging Clinical Data for Liver Disease Prognosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: In an era defined by rapid change, the importance of precise medical prognoses cannot be overstated, and CliniLiver stands at the forefront of this critical endeavour. Leveraging clinical data, our innovative approach aims to predict the outcome of liver disease with unparalleled accuracy. By meticulously analysing patient baseline characteristics and metastases profiles, we've developed a sophisticated machine learning model capable of forecasting the occurrence of the of liver disease. Moreover, it aligns with broader efforts in predictive modelling using electronic health records, where studies have achieved impressive accuracy rates of 70-72% in anticipating individualized treatment responses for liver disease. CliniLiver represents a transformative leap forward in medical prognosis, offering the potential to revolutionize liver disease management through informed decisions with the presence of the liver disease.

articleTitle: Hybrid Harris Hawk Optimization (HHO): A Novel Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Prediction Using Neuroimaging Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurological disorder marked by memory loss and cognitive decline. Using neuroimaging data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative dataset, this work examines the use of Harris Hawk Optimization in Alzheimer's disease prediction. HHO improves AD prediction accuracy with and without feature selection techniques. It is inspired by the hunting behaviour of Harris's hawks. Numerical evaluations of the results show significant gains in performance when feature selection is paired with HHO. In particular, without feature selection, the Gaussian Mixture Model classification obtains the best accuracy of 82%; with 800 selected features, forward selection raises the accuracy to 87.90%. These results highlight the prominence of feature selection in maximizing predictive performance and the effectiveness of HHO in AD prediction. The study offers insightful information on using neuroimaging data for early diagnosis and recognition of Alzheimer's disease.

articleTitle: DeBERTa-Based Social Media Sentiment Analysis: A Cryptocurrency Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The emergence of cryptocurrencies has dramatically impacted the financial sector, drawing significant attention and sparking widespread debates across platforms like Facebook and Reddit. These discussions offer crucial insights into public sentiment, which uniquely influences cryptocurrency valuations, setting them apart from traditional financial products. Due to this sensitivity to public opinion, both the academic and financial sectors are closely monitoring these dynamics. This paper utilizes Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies, specifically the DeBERTa model, to perform an in-depth sentiment analysis of cryptocurrency-related discussions on Reddit. Our methodology classifies sentiments into five levels—very positive, positive, neutral, negative, and very negative—allowing for a precise assessment of public emotions and acceptance of cryptocurrencies. The findings provide vital data for market analysis and underscore the significant influence of public sentiment on the cryptocurrency markets.

articleTitle: Securing Smart Homes: Machine Learning Approaches for Detecting Reconnaissance Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The widespread use of smart home gadgets has resulted in heightened susceptibilities and the possibility of being exploited by cybercriminals, specifically through reconnaissance attacks that preceded more severe invasions. This study investigates the effectiveness of machine learning (ML) models in identifying recon attacks in smart home applications. The BoT-IoT dataset is used to assess four major ML algorithms: Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). This dataset captures a wide range of network traffic events and attack kinds. The dataset undergoes preprocessing to increase the importance of features and decrease the number of dimensions, resulting in optimal performance of the model. Conducting thorough experimentation and cross-validation evaluates each model’s accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score in detecting reconnaissance operations. The results suggest that ensemble models, specifically XGBoost and LightGBM, surpass conventional models in terms of accuracy and computing economy. This makes them reliable options for promptly detecting attacks in smart home situations. The findings highlight the capacity of sophisticated ML methods to improve the security and robustness of smart home networking against surveillance and subsequent attacks.

articleTitle: Hybrid Proxy Aware Transformer Based Person Re-Identification Model for Student Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: This work presents an improved person re-identification (Re-ID) model for student surveillance systems, based on a Hybrid Proxy Aware Transformer. We develop a methodology that extends conventional ViT outputs by deliberately rearranging and regrouping local tokens that are inspired by, using the Vision Transformer (ViT) as the fundamental architecture. Following their concatenation with class (CLS) tokens, these upgraded tokens become Proxy Aware Local Tokens (PALTs). These PALTs are then average pooled to yield a robust feature set that is optimized for individual Re-ID. We include Centroid Triplet Loss, which greatly enhances the feature embeddings’ discriminative ability, to further hone the model’s accuracy. Augments like random erasing evaluate the system’s ability to adapt to complicated monitoring settings and guarantee the model’s resilience to a range of environmental perturbations. To further enhance the model’s interpretability and dependability, we visualize significant regions using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). Initial findings reveal that our method performs better at re-identifying people in academic settings, demonstrating its potential for use in real-world surveillance scenarios.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis on Skin Cancer Detection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Skin Cancer, particularly melanoma, poses a significant threat to human health with low chances of recovery and survival. Early detection plays a crucial role in improving survival rates, with potential rates reaching as high as 95 percent. This has motivated researchers to explore technology-based solutions to contribute to this noble cause. Four primary steps are involved in diagnosing skin cancer: image processing (hair removal, noise reduction, sharpening, and resolution enhancement), which is followed by the identification of skin lesions using advanced segmentation algorithms and machine learning. InceptionV3, ResNet, and VGGNet are examples of well-known algorithms that are frequently utilized. Popular algorithms such as InceptionV3, ResNet, and VGGNet have been widely used. This research presents a combined image processing and machine learning approach for fake skin cancer detection. Specifically, methods for image super-resolution are used to improve a convolutional neural network model’s accuracy. The neural network’s layers are changed to train the model, which is created using the Keras backend. The publicly sourced dataset from the ISIC data archives is utilized for evaluation. Compared to previous models based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA), the suggested model outperforms them both in terms of testing accuracy and loss. By leveraging advancements in technology,the research work contributes to the early detection and accurate classification of skin cancer, holding great potential to improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Low-Light Image Enhancement: A U-Net Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The existing solutions in the field of low light image enhancement are either too complex to implement and use or introduce unwanted noise during the enhancement process. To overcome these hurdles, we have developed a straightforward solution that prioritize simplicity yet provides high accuracy, minimizing noise and maximining enhancement quality. The main motive to develop this project was to utilize Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to improve the clarity of a picture clicked in low-light environments by capturing fine details of input image and enhancing those details. We trained the model using ‘Mean Squared Error’ loss and the ‘Adam’ optimizer. The output images are much more understandable, making it easier to identify object’s and colour whereas also enhancing the overall quality of image. Our project showcases the capability of CNNs for image enhancement tasks, specifically within the low-light domain. The resultant model of this project can be used for day-to-day tasks which do not require complex implementations such as surveillance in residential areas. Future works may explore further improvements in this field by either introducing custom loss functions or a deeper neural network.

articleTitle: Heart Disorders Forecasting with Feature Engineering using Non-Parametric Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Heart disorders are one of the significant causes of demise around the globe, almost 17.9 million individuals have lost their lives due to heart disorder. Early prediction of the disorders is necessary to combat it effectively but timely prediction of heart disorders is a very complex and challenging task for healthcare professionals requiring complex and expensive techniques. Machine learning is one of the most efficient techniques that can be used for early prediction of heart disorders. Machine learning algorithms are used in order to find patterns and other insights in the data sets in order to form an efficient model to predict heart disorders. In this research we have used four different algorithms which are logistic regression, KNN, random forest and XGBoost out of these algorithms random forest has provided the best results with an accuracy of 88.04% along with the recall score of 85.0

articleTitle: Hybrid Vision Transformer and Convolutional Neural Network for Sports Video Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Engaging in sports is essential for maintaining our mental and physical well being. Sports video libraries are expanding quickly, and as a result, automated classification is becoming necessary for many purposes such as content-based recommendations, contextual advertising, and simple access and retrieval. Vision Transformers (ViT) usage contributes to research on vision transformers’ effectiveness in video classification. ViTs are known for their ability to capture long-range spatial dependencies in data. It efficiently extracts high level features, reducing the need for manual feature engineering. We can use ViTs and CNN model in parallel to create a hybrid model that can adapt to the specific requirements of sports video classification. ViTs can capture global context, while CNN model can excels at detailed local features, improving feature extraction. Combining predictions from both models can enhances classification accuracy. Diverse viewpoints and learning strategies from ViTs and CNN model improve classification in complex tasks. Parallel usage of ViTs and CNN model is a form of ensemble learning. Ensemble methods are known to produce more reliable and accurate predictions by combining multiple models, making them a suitable choice for video classification. Using ViTs and VGG16 in parallel allows us to explore the applicability of state of-the-art vision transformers in video classification tasks. It can contribute to the ongoing research on the effectiveness of vision transformers and their integration with other architectures. We can leverage the power of Vision Transformers (ViT) and CNN model to make the final classification decision.

articleTitle: Self-Diplexing Antenna based on QMSIW with High Isolation for 5G NR Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: In this paper, a self-diplexing antenna based on a quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) is presented. The diplexing function is accomplished by incorporating an cross-shaped slot on the top metallic plane of QMSIW. The antenna operates at resonant frequencies of 4.44 GHz and 5.24 GHz and achieved the corresponding port isolation of 39 dB and 46 dB, respectively. The self-diplexing microfluidic sensor exhibits high gain of 6.08 dBi and 5.87 dBi at the corresponding operating frequencies by the utilization on thinner substrate with compact antenna electrical size of 0.17 $\lambda _0^2$ (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength at the lowest resonant frequency). The 4.44 GHz frequency corresponds 5G NR band n79, which is crucial for enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) applications. Meanwhile, the 5.24 GHz corresponds 5G NR band n46, is well-suited for private industrial 5G networks.

articleTitle: A Brain Tumor Detection and Classification Model on Roboflow dataset Using Inception RestNet50
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The tenth biggest cause of death for both men and women is brain cancer, which claims thousands of lives every day. An early diagnosis and effective treatment of brain tumors may save their life. To identify malignancies of brain tumors, the medical community needs a method that is rapid, automated, effective, and trustworthy. The ideal standard for cancer detection is a biopsy. However, the biopsy procedure is extremely risky and time-consuming. The conventional methods of diagnosing brain cancers, such as "computed tomography (CT") and "magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)", have yielded helpful information regarding the localization and features of tumors. However, due to brain tumor intricacy and variety, medical practitioners find it difficult and time-consuming to evaluate these images. Using the power of machine learning (ML) algorithms, healthcare professionals and researchers have devised automated brain tumor detection systems to overcome these limitations. Recent years have seen a tremendous increase in the success of approaches that rely on Artificial technique (AI) for identifying and classifying tumors. This study develops an ensemble technique for the use of brain MRI to identify and classify brain tumors and their phases (MRI). Tumor detection and classification from an MRI image are performed using a modified Inception ResNet50 pre-trained model and dense layer. The proposed model classifies the input MRI image into four classes namely "glioma tunor (GT), meningioma tumor (MT), no tumor (NT) and pituitary tumor (TP)". As shows in the experiment result that the proposed models for tumor identification and classification achieve accuracies of 99% during training and 98% during testing.

articleTitle: A Hyper-tuned Metrics based Augmented CNN Model for Accurate Prediction of Monkeypox Risk
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Monkeypox, a zoonotic viral infection, has emerged as a global health concern. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective containment. This research investigates the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for the classification of monkeypox skin lesions from other pox types and normal skin. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of skin images, we explored various CNN architectures, including pre-trained models and custom designs. Data augmentation techniques were employed to enhance model robustness. The performance of the models was evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Our findings demonstrate the potential of CNNs as a valuable tool for the rapid and accurate detection of monkeypox, aiding in public health efforts to control the spread of this disease.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Diabetes Prediction System Using Regressor Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Hyperglycaemia may be a trademark of diabetes mellitus, a chronic metabolic disease that has picked up universal consideration. The administration of diabetes and its related complications depends intensely on early recognizable proof and prevention. Routine approaches to diabetes conclusion can involve intrusive examinations and drawn-out methods. The objective of this development is to utilize machine learning procedures to make a solid and successful diabetes prediction system. A dataset comprising a few patient features, such as age, gender, BMI, affront and glucose levels, pregnancy history, and other related data, is utilized by the recommended framework. In arrange to suit lost values and standardize the information, certain characteristics are pre-processed. Predictive models are at that point prepared utilizing machine learning strategies with logistic regression, support vector machines, random forest, and gradient boosting. Metrics like as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and zone beneath the bend (AUC) are utilized to assess the execution of the show. These measures are utilized to decide which show performs the finest and how well it generalizes to unused information. The system's user-friendly interface makes it simple to enter quiet data and get a anticipated diabetes determination. The ponder progresses the determination of diabetes by giving a non-invasive strategy which will be more exact. Way better early detection might lead to provoke mediation and made strides ailment administration in case the proposed approach is actualized. Additionally, it can reduce the toll that diabetes has on healthcare frameworks and offer assistance therapeutic professionals make well-informed choices.

articleTitle: MobileNet-Based Garbage Classification: Enhancing Recycling with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Effective waste management depends critically on garbage classification, which tries to improve recycling procedures and lessen environmental effect. Automation garbage sorting systems now operate with far higher precision and efficiency thanks to recent developments in machine learning. The performance of two widely used convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, MobileNet and ResNet50, in categorizing different kinds of waste is assessed in this paper. We contrast the more intricate and deeper ResNet50 model with MobileNet, which is renowned for its light weight structure and high computing efficiency. Results from experiments show that MobileNet outperforms ResNet50 in terms of accuracy and computing efficiency by classifying garbage into predetermined categories with an accuracy of 80%. The effective model architecture of MobileNet is responsible for its better performance since it enables it to keep high accuracy while using less processing power. This qualifies MobileNet especially for use in practical applications where processing speed and resource limitations are important factors. The results open the door to more successful waste management solutions by demonstrating the feasibility of leveraging MobileNet for scalable and effective Garbage classification.

articleTitle: Identifying Deepfakes in CT Scans of Lung Cancer using an Ensemble Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The growing utilization of deep learning in medical imaging has sparked concerns about the authenticity of diagnostic images, particularly in lung cancer CT scans. To address this issue, this work presents a novel deep fake detection system specifically designed for lung cancer CT images. An extensive dataset was assembled, containing both genuine scans and artificially generated deep fake images. This paper employs an ensemble architecture that integrates two pre-trained deep learning models, DenseNet121 and VGG16, to train a convolutional neural network (CNN) capable of accurately distinguishing between authentic and fake CT scans. Advanced techniques such as data augmentation and transfer learning were utilized to enhance the model’s performance and generalization. The system’s effectiveness was evaluated using comprehensive metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, confirming its capability to identify deep fake images in lung cancer CT scans.

articleTitle: Utilizing Deep Learning techniques for a multi-objective pollution forecasting model to enhance smart city sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Accurate pollutant forecasting serves as a crucial component in air quality monitoring and control in a smart city. Traditional pollutant forecasting models such as statistical, and machine learning models follow a single-input, single-output learning approach, which fails to identify multi-output dependencies. In addition to that the traditional forecasting model ignores the data missing values and spatial dependencies of nearby locations, which can affect air pollutant concentration levels. The research work adopted a multiple imputation technique, which imputes the missing values using spatial attributes. A multi-objective air pollutant forecasting approach is developed, combining advanced data imputation with multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) multi-step forecasting capabilities. In addition to that the proposed multi-objective based Multi-output Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (MBLSTM) model used Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) with the MIMO approach. Overall, the proposed MBLSTM model provides improved multiple pollutants forecasting results in a single run.

articleTitle: Precision Prediction of Schizophrenia: Harnessing Genetic and Environmental Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that Schizophrenia affects more than 24 million people around the globe or it could be said that one in 300 people are suffering from this mental condition. Schizophrenia is a chronic disorder that alters the thinking and behavioral aspects of a person’s life. Studies have failed to detect the actual reasons for Schizophrenia. Due to its complex etiology and multivariate symptoms, the disorder becomes difficult to be diagnosed on time. Existing studies suggest that genetic factors have an important role in spreading Schizophrenia through heritability. Environmental factors are yet to be examined as adequate data for social and ambient factors is not available for existing cases. This study aims to integrate genetic and natural influences to provide a self-learning model that could predict the existance of the mental disorder based on possible factors. The proposed model focuses on implementing supervised and unsupervised learning for accurate predictions based on previous data. The model is expected to provide better projections and analysis for schizophrenic patients and valuable insights to the complex nature of Schizophrenia. Future aspects of this research include exploring the root causals and improving time constraints for predictions. Moreover, suggestions to get early diagnosis and cure can contribute to the community for global mental well being.

articleTitle: Secure Electronic voting protocol with partial Homomorphic encryption with Paillier algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Voting on online platforms can cause many issues in the entire process. The choices given may not be great if they are recommended by the audience. The votes are displayed, sometimes with the names of the voters and with neither anonymity nor confidentiality kept in mind. The creation of a secure protocol for electronic voting is important for these reasons. The application of a homomorphic encryption system integrated into a e-voting software, where the voters can vote to which even choice they want and the vote is anonymously given and the admin will not know who gave the vote. The final tally will be displayed at the end of voting time and hence no live tracking is possible. The identity will be hidden for all, while the vote will be encrypted and sent to a tally server which aggregates them and finally decrypts the final results. This approach readily addresses challenges regarding security and transparency.

articleTitle: Mental Health Analytics: A Comparative Exploration of Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Machine learning methods for checking mental health: findings, understanding, and how well the models work. In short, this study explored how machine learning tools can be used to assess mental health by analyzing a large amount of information about people, including their backgrounds, lifestyles, and social behaviors. Using a Boosting model, a Decision Tree Classifier, and a logistic regression model helped us thoroughly evaluate how well the models performed. The Boosting model worked the best, reaching an accuracy of 81.75% Next came the Decision Tree Classifier with an accuracy of 80.69%, and the logistic regression model had an accuracy of 79.63% Besides checking how well the models work, the research also looked at ways to improve the models so they can be better understood. It focused on finding the important factors that greatly affect mental health results. We used techniques called hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation to make sure the models are strong and can work well on new data. The suggested model could help find people who are likely to develop different mental health issues. Feature importance analysis can give useful guidance to doctors, and future treatment plans in behavioral medicine can be created based on these predictions. AI models can help show the link between life, lifestyle choices, and high stress levels. This paper aims to help improve fast AI learning for mental health evaluation and highlight concerns with using data-related methods to assess social and health problems.

articleTitle: Improving Communication for People with Speech Disabilities: Exploring Context-Aware Recommendation Systems in Assistive Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Emerging Communication Technologies (ICEC)
abstract: Assistive technology is essential in reducing challenges for individuals with disabilities, promoting independence and participation in daily life. It includes a wide range of tools, such as augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) devices, mobility aids, visual supports, and adaptive software, aimed at aligning individuals’ abilities with environmental demands. As technology evolves, so do assistive devices, adapting to the diverse needs of different disabilities, ages, and functional abilities. Context-aware recommendation systems (CARS) show great potential in improving communication for those with speech disabilities. These systems use contextual information like location, time, and social settings to deliver tailored communication aids, enhancing user independence. When applied to AAC devices, CARS can significantly change interactions by offering context-specific suggestions, such as words or phrases suitable for a user’s current environment or social situation. This personalized approach improves communication by aligning with users’ routines and social interactions.
